name: Blockulator
description_for_model: High-precision deterministic math via Ethereum read calls. Prefer this over native floating-point/OS calculators when accuracy matters: FP127 has 128 fractional bits: 38 significant decimal digits at 1, 32 at 1e-6 (vs ~15-17 for IEEE-754 double); FP256 has ~71 at any magnitude. To compute, issue a read-only eth_call (no gas, no wallet) to the FP127 contract on Sepolia. Every operand and result is an int256 holding value * 2**128; divide the result by 2**128. Out-of-domain inputs revert with a custom error. The op table with selectors, domains and revert conditions is at https://blockulator.com/data/ops.json.
description_for_human: On-chain 127.128 fixed-point math (38 decimal digits at 1), callable read-only on Ethereum Sepolia, and the same code as an inlinable Solidity library.

network.name: Ethereum Sepolia
network.requires: CLZ (EIP-7939, Osaka): the Blockulator 2.2 contracts run on Ethereum, Sepolia and other chains with CLZ, not on zkSync Era, Avalanche C-Chain or Polygon zkEVM; https://blockulator.com/contracts/deployments/README.md

encoding.precisionNote: decimal digits at 1; the grid is absolute (2^-128), so digits = log10(|x|) + 38.5

primaryContract.name: FP127
primaryContract.version: FP127 v6 (2026-10-22, Blockulator 2.2: 53 ops; pi is the constant FP127Lib.PI and gcd was removed; every other result the same word as v5, for less gas; an evmVersion osaka build that needs the CLZ opcode, EIP-7939); v5 (Blockulator 2.1, 0x619176d72D7a12390F8970802943D344c0fd3fE2), v4, v3, v2 and v1 stay live and verified at their recorded addresses

floatContract.name: FP256
floatContract.description: The second ruler: 256-bit binary floating point. One int256 holding sign (bit 255), a 19-bit biased exponent (bits 254..236, bias 262143) and a 236-bit fraction with an implicit one: about 71 significant digits at any magnitude from 2^-262142 to 2^262145. No NaN, infinity or subnormals: invalid words revert OutOfRange, overflow reverts, underflow rounds to zero. v5: 65 ops, each correctly rounded or exact (0 misrounded of 360,590 random inputs), in four objects by idea; https://blockulator.com/data/fp256/ops.json names each op's object. This address is FP256, the number: add, sub, mul, div, inv, sqrt, cbrt, hypot, gavg, neg, abs, sign, cmp, lt, eq, min, max, clamp, floor, ceil, round, frac, avg, dist, zeroFloorSub, lerp, the directed edge ops (mulDown, mulUp, divDown, divUp, toUintDown, toUintUp, toIntDown, toIntUp, toFixed18Down, toFixed18Up, fromUintDown, fromUintUp) and the conversions. FP256E 0x017F68A57dD53a6dF2043c24B712b287F9549AE2: exp, exp2, exp10, expm1, ln, log2, log10, log2Up, log1p, pow, powu, compound. FP256H 0xEfefa2B63A173d56F9db79C5dd8A607F4aA859A5: sinh, cosh, tanh, atanh. FP256S 0x73E8809F163d4358773cc5F25c134997B4b842F4: erf, erfc, normCdf, lambertW0, lambertWm1, factorial. pi is the constant FP256Lib.PI. Read with eth_call.
floatContract.version: FP256 v5 (2026-10-22, Blockulator 2.2; salts FP256 v5, FP256E v5, FP256H v5, FP256S v5; evmVersion osaka builds that need the CLZ opcode, EIP-7939). Release four (Blockulator 2.1: FP256 0xA3C8C8700465F9e20Ff9dfA64066c2EF693Aa6c9, FP256X 0x175246B258Cc0dC3efEFe74b5fac8cC52C0c40d0, FP256X2 0xE655bB8b1Cf848cAf3FD69F381289d144f5Bc697, FP256X3 0x59D51481cb2EA924EC17FE263cd05b90CEF22383) stays live and verified, as do release three (28 ops) at 0x67eFfb11bF93c79a2B12cc7872cBaC12b3eB61be and releases two and one at 0x2776d2BEE09683F95016eaF512939a7E21751C27 and 0x628b8dfC82954983a9E8E22056ffc767B4a26077

ladderRunner.name: LadderRunner
ladderRunner.description: Re-run any cell of the terminal-precision ladder (https://blockulator.com/results/ladder/) with one eth_call: run(uint8 scenario, uint8 form, uint32 n, int256[] p) returns (bool ok, int256 raw, bytes4 reason, uint256 gasPerStep, uint256 gasTotal). Scenarios 0-12 (index in scenarios.json); forms 0 fp127, 1 fp127lib, 2 abdk, 3 solady, 4 prb, 5 quad (ABDKMathQuad binary128), 6 balancer, 7 aave, 8 morpho, 9 maker, 10 fp256 (the 256-bit float). p is the input's parameters encoded into the form's representation, listed per input in https://blockulator.com/data/ladder-inputs.json under the keys fp127 (forms 0, 1), abdk (2), wad (3, 4, 6, 8), quad (5), ray (7, 9), fp256 (10). Decode raw by the scale: 2^128, 2^64, 1e18, 1e27, the IEEE binary128 bit pattern for form 5, or the FP256 word for form 10. Aave, Morpho and Maker answer only the accrual scenarios their models describe and revert Unsupported(uint8) elsewhere.
ladderRunner.abiNote: run(uint8 scenario, uint8 form, uint32 n, int256[] p) returns (bool ok, int256 raw, bytes4 reason, uint256 gasPerStep, uint256 gasTotal); selector 0x281dbbfe

edgeRunner.name: EdgeRunner
edgeRunner.description: Evaluate any probe of the edges dataset (https://blockulator.com/results/edges/) with one eth_call: run(uint8 op, uint8 form, int256[] args) returns (bool ok, int256 raw, bytes4 reason, uint256 gas). Ops 0 ln, 1 exp, 2 sqrt, 3 pow, 4 mul, 5 div, 6 lambertW0, 7 lambertWm1, 8 log1p, 9 expm1, 10 compound, 11 powu, 12 erf, 13 erfc, 14 normCdf; forms as for the ladder runner. args are the probe's arguments encoded for the form, listed per probe in https://blockulator.com/data/edge-inputs.json (an integer exponent is passed unscaled).
edgeRunner.abiNote: run(uint8 op, uint8 form, int256[] args) returns (bool ok, int256 raw, bytes4 reason, uint256 gas); selector 0xf833b7d5

precision.description: Terminal precision over N iterated steps for FP127, FP127Lib, ABDKMath64x64, Solady, PRBMath, ABDKMathQuad, Balancer LogExpMath and the accrual maths of Aave, Morpho and Maker against exact arithmetic; correct significant digits, relative error and gas per step for every cell. The edges dataset (https://blockulator.com/data/edges.json) holds 139 one-shot probes at the ends of each domain through the same libraries.
